problems.text: Buses arrive at a stop according to a Poisson process with an average rate of 4 buses per hour. You arrive at the stop at a uniformly random time. What is your expected waiting time until the next bus, in minutes? Give a single number.

On a game show there are 3 doors: one hides a car, two hide goats. You pick a door. The host, who has forgotten where the car is, trips and accidentally opens one of the other two doors completely at random - and it happens to reveal a goat. You are offered the chance to switch to the remaining unopened door. Given what has happened, what is the probability that switching wins the car? Give a single number.

A family is selected uniformly at random from all two-child families (each child independently equally likely to be a boy or girl, and born on each of the 7 weekdays with equal probability). You learn that this family has at least one boy who was born on a Tuesday. What is the probability that both children are boys? Give a single number.

A school has exactly three classes, with 10, 20, and 90 students respectively (120 students total). A student is selected uniformly at random from the 120 students and asked the size of their class. What is the expected value of their answer? Give a single number.
You flip a fair coin repeatedly. What is the expected number of flips until you first see the pattern HH (two heads in a row, on consecutive flips)? Give a single number.

You will interview 4 candidates one at a time in uniformly random order. After each interview you can rank the candidate against those already seen, and must immediately accept or reject them; rejections are final. You use the following strategy: reject the first candidate, then accept the first subsequent candidate who is better than everyone seen so far (if none, you must accept the last candidate). What is the probability you accept the single best candidate of the 4? Give a single number.

A casino game: a fair coin is flipped until it first lands heads, but at most 10 flips. If the first head appears on flip k (for k from 1 to 10), you win 2^k dollars. If no head appears in the 10 flips, you win nothing. What is the expected value of your winnings in dollars? Give a single number.

A gambler starts with 2 dollars and repeatedly plays a game where each round they win 1 dollar with probability 0.6 and lose 1 dollar with probability 0.4, independently. They stop when they reach 5 dollars or go broke at 0 dollars. What is the probability they reach 5 dollars? Give a single number.

You roll a fair six-sided die repeatedly until you roll the first 6, then stop. Consider only those experiments in which every roll made (including the final 6) was an even number. Conditioned on that event, what is the expected total number of rolls? Give a single number.

In a country, every family has children one at a time until their first boy is born, then stops having children. Each birth is independently a boy or a girl with probability 1/2. In the long run, what fraction of all children in the country are boys? Give a single number.

A disease has 1% prevalence. A test has 90% sensitivity (positive if diseased) and 90% specificity (negative if healthy). A person takes the test twice, and the two results are conditionally independent given their true disease status. Both tests come back positive. What is the probability the person has the disease? Give a single number.

Two evenly matched teams (each wins any given game independently with probability 1/2) play a best-of-seven series: the series ends as soon as one team has won 4 games. What is the expected total number of games played? Give a single number.
